render.note: The verdicts below were measured with cybergate_mode=baseline, NO system prompt and max_tokens=1. Baseline mode skips the steering route but not the probe or the gate, so the worker still writes a full decision record. A different render shifts the scores: a matched split of a never-sent corpus showed a measurable median shift between with-system and no-system arms, so send the canaries exactly as described here.

assertion: expect_fired must match the decision record's `fired` for every canary
provenance: Positives only. The shipped operator's own metadata records 100/100 fit positives firing raw on the served checkpoint, which licenses a per-prompt fire expectation for any of them. It also records 17/140 fit references firing but not which 17, so no negative canary can be asserted without re-measuring. These five keys are the first five by key order -- not selected by margin, because per-prompt Qwen scores were never harvested at this layer and threshold.
known_gaps: No negative canaries. Needs one Qwen serve to harvest fit_ref_140 per prompt.
No per-prompt margins, so a near-threshold positive could flip under a render change and look like a checkpoint mismatch. If these fail, harvest all 100 before concluding.
